svg.title: Visual abstract: how loss of MYORG reshapes the astrocyte transcriptome
svg.desc: Primary cortical and cerebellar astrocytes from wild-type and Myorg knockout mice were grown with or without serum (27 RNA-seq libraries, 8 groups, 12 contrasts) and analysed with STAR, edgeR, limma-voom, fgsea and clusterProfiler. Without serum, Myorg knockout astrocytes show lower apoptosis and oxidative phosphorylation signatures in cortex but higher ones in cerebellum, and NF-kB inflammatory signaling is raised in serum-free conditions.
svg.text: VISUAL ABSTRACT · BULK RNA-SEQ · PRIMARY FAMILIAL BRAIN CALCIFICATION (PFBC)
How loss of MYORG reshapes the astrocyte transcriptome
Primary mouse astrocytes · wild-type vs Myorg−/− · cortex vs cerebellum · with vs without serum
In PFBC, calcium phosphate builds up
in the basal ganglia, thalamus and
cerebellum. MYORG is an ER enzyme
sequencing run kept in the model.
Apoptosis and OxPhos fall in cortex
Bash on an HPC cluster (SLURM), then R / Bioconductor
Without Myorg, serum-starved astrocytes turn on NF-κB inflammation, while cell-death and energy
programs move in opposite directions in cortex and cerebellum: one mutation, region-specific astrocyte responses.
